take_homes: Having a licence is not the same as people using the tool. I want both numbers side by side, not one.
Before I judge a tool, find out what people use today and what would make them drop it.
A plan with unnamed owners is not a plan. Ask who owns it, in names.

monday.move: Pull usage against licence count for the two or three AI tools we already pay for. Then ask my controller one question: how does she do the month-end variance commentary today?
monday.who: My controller, plus IT for the usage numbers
monday.when: Monday morning, before the leadership meeting
monday.stop_condition: If the usage data takes IT more than a day to produce, I drop it and tell the CEO the data doesn't exist.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved any tool for finance data, so even a test on our numbers is not allowed yet.

misconception.why: I walked in thinking AI is a licence you buy. The point that access is one switch and use takes weeks made me doubt that. I still don't see what this costs per head or what it returns, so I haven't changed my mind.

one_line: One good idea, that licences are not usage, repeated through a lot of filler, and nowhere a cost or payback figure I could take to the board.
